entries.title: SEC Trading and Markets staff statement discloses four Form 1-N security futures product exchange registrations, footnoted as Coinbase Derivatives, KalshiEX, Bitnomial and Nadex, and invites comment on exchange affiliations with broker-dealers
entries.facts: The SEC Division of Trading and Markets published a "Staff Statement on Affiliations Between National Securities Exchanges and Broker-Dealers" dated Sept. 30, 2026. The statement says the Commission "recently received four Form 1-Ns for notice registration as security futures product exchanges under Section 6(g) of the Exchange Act" and that each registrant "discloses in its Form 1-N that it is affiliated with an FCM that will perform introducing broker functions, extend margin to customers and hold client funds and property, and is a member of the exchange for purposes of trading security futures." The page's footnotes identify the four registrants as Coinbase Derivatives, LLC; KalshiEX LLC; Bitnomial Exchange, LLC; and North American Derivatives Exchange, Inc. The statement says that "the financial interests of the national securities exchange may conflict with its responsibilities as an SRO regarding the affiliated broker-dealer," and that the staff "invites comment from market participants regarding national securities exchange affiliations, including with entities that engage in broker activity on behalf of customers on the exchange or that trade in a principal capacity on the exchange." No comment deadline or closing date is stated on the page. The statement carries the disclaimer that it "represents the views of the Staff" and "is not a rule, regulation, guidance, or statement of the Commission."
entries.source_label: SEC Division of Trading and Markets, staff statement, Sept. 30, 2026
entries.relevant_to: crypto derivatives exchanges, prediction-market platforms, futures commission merchants, broker-dealers

entries.title: FTC advance notice of proposed rulemaking on the Rule on Impersonation of Government and Businesses publishes in the Federal Register with comments due November 30, 2026
entries.facts: Federal Register document 2026-20143, an FTC advance notice of proposed rulemaking and request for public comment titled "Rule on Impersonation of Government and Businesses," RIN 3084-AB90, Matter No. R207000, 16 CFR part 461, published October 1, 2026. Its DATES section reads: "Comments must be received on or before November 30, 2026." Its SUMMARY states that the Commission "proposes to commence a rulemaking proceeding to prevent certain unfair or deceptive acts or practices by search engine, social media, and other digital marketplace platforms that further government and business impersonation scams to defraud consumers" and that it "is soliciting written comment, data, and arguments concerning the need for such rulemaking." The document states that platforms offer "ad-optimization tools and services that enhance an ad's effectiveness," naming among them "ad copy creation, image and video generation, ad enhancements," and discusses how platforms "profit from optimizing online ads for third parties." Dollar figures carried in the document include approximately $16 billion in consumer fraud losses in 2025, an estimated true fraud cost of $195.9 billion in 2024, nearly $3.5 billion in reported impersonation losses, and $2.1 billion in reported social media scam losses in 2025.
entries.source_label: Federal Register document 2026-20143, FTC advance notice of proposed rulemaking, Oct. 1, 2026
entries.relevant_to: payment processors, fintech consumer brands, advertising platforms, marketplaces

entries.title: The three remaining orders in the SEC's September 30 block against crypto-funded offshore contract-for-differences brokerages name a fourth platform, FxSway, and impose a further $190,000 in penalties
entries.facts: Three further settled administrative orders in the SEC's sequential September 30, 2026 block were retrieved in full. Release 34-106541 (File No. 3-22762) finds that Lewis Neal, age 31, of Celina, Texas, operated FxSway LLC, an unregistered online brokerage incorporated in St. Vincent and the Grenadines at www.fxsway.com, from 2021 to 2023, and states that "customers registered on the FxSway website, funded their trading accounts with Bitcoin or other crypto assets that were custodied in a margin account." It finds a willful violation of Section 15(a)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 for effecting unregistered broker transactions in security-based swaps in the form of stock-based contracts for differences, and imposes a cease-and-desist order, a two year associational bar with a right to apply for reentry, and a $60,000 civil money penalty payable within 10 days. Release 34-106542 (File No. 3-22763) makes parallel findings against Michael Levi Peters, age 32, of Houston, Texas, as to Prosperity LLC at www.prosperity4x.com for 2020 to 2023, with the same funding sentence and a $65,000 penalty due within 10 days. Release 34-106543 (File No. 3-22764) makes parallel findings against Michael Talento, age 32, of San Marcos, California, as to the same Prosperity LLC and website for 2020 to 2023, with the same funding sentence and a $65,000 penalty payable in three installments of $13,000 within 10 days, $13,000 within 180 days, and the remainder within 365 days. All three impose two year associational bars with a right to apply for reentry.
entries.source_label: SEC administrative order, Release 34-106541, File No. 3-22762, Sept. 30, 2026
entries.relevant_to: crypto-funded trading venues, contract-for-differences platforms, offshore brokerages, affiliate marketers

entries.title: SEC announces final judgments against three BitConnect promoters, directing disgorgement, prejudgment interest and civil penalties together with permanent injunctions
entries.facts: SEC Litigation Release No. 26660, dated September 30, 2026, concerns Securities and Exchange Commission v. Brown et al., No. 1:21-cv-04791 (S.D.N.Y. filed May 28, 2021). The release states that three individuals promoted BitConnect between June 2017 and January 2018, marketing and selling securities in its "lending program," and that the SEC charged they "offered and sold the securities without registering the securities offering" or operating as registered broker-dealers, in violation of Section 5 of the Securities Act of 1933 and Section 15(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. Three final judgments are reported. Michael Noble, judgment entered July 17, 2026: disgorgement of $731,281, prejudgment interest of $293,703.36 and a civil penalty of $50,000, a total of $1,074,984.36, with permanent injunctions. Craig Grant, judgment entered August 7, 2026: disgorgement of $1,748,147, prejudgment interest of $702,105.84 and a civil penalty of $230,480, a total of $2,680,732.84, with permanent injunctions. Trevon Brown, judgment entered September 9, 2026: disgorgement of $1,728,563, prejudgment interest of $182,902.15 and a civil penalty of $75,000, a total of $1,986,465.15, with permanent injunctions.
entries.relevant_to: token promoters, affiliate and referral marketers, crypto lending platforms, influencers
